title: Radiance as Service
author: Kathleen Schafer
summary: Schafer argues that leadership at its core is a generosity of presence: a leader who is grounded and aligned steadies the people around them. She leans on the claim that emotional states are contagious, so a centered leader calms and clarifies a team while a wavering one spreads confusion. The central move is to tie the leader's own alignment, saying what is true and then acting consistently with it, to the health of the whole organization. She diagnoses much social disharmony as the gap between what people say and what they do, and asks leaders to notice that gap with neutrality rather than a gotcha spirit. The piece closes with a week-long invitation and reflection questions, in her usual devotional register.
points: Leadership is framed as generosity of presence, so the leader's inner steadiness is itself the service offered to a team.
Emotional states are contagious, which means a leader's calm or anxiety entrains everyone around them.
Misalignment between words and actions is named as the engine of organizational and social discord.
The practice she asks for is noticing misalignment with clarity and neutrality, in oneself first, rather than policing others.
quotes: It is the choice to let our clarity soothe confusion, our steadiness calm fear, and our groundedness invite coherence.
You cannot help others find clarity if you are abandoning your own. You cannot hold steady in truth if you are wavering within yourself.
Much of the disharmony in our society today arises because people are saying one thing and doing another.
When truth is unspoken, problems multiply. When we refuse to illuminate what is real, we end up addressing only the surface, never the source.
Radiance as service begins with walking your talk. It continues by seeing clearly where others are not.
